title: The Compass of Manchester's mill district
premise: In 1848, Mirabel Underhill carries sealed dispatches for a republic already falling, believing herself a mere courier in a quiet mill district of Manchester. When a stranger arrives bearing a letter in the handwriting of her brother—declared dead two years past—she discovers the dispatches conceal a treaty that could save the exiled government, and that her own workshop is the last place its terms can be decoded. Betrayed by the man she trusted and hunted by agents of the old regime, she must finish the decoding before the morning tide takes the ship that carries both the treaty and the truth about her brother. She succeeds at terrible cost: the republic is beyond saving, but the treaty secures refuge for its survivors, and Mirabel chooses to stay behind, finally belonging to the city and people she once thought were merely a stop on someone else's history.
about_author: Hazel Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing exile correspondence in northern English county records. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught inside extraordinary paperwork.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Paper
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She delivers routine dispatches through Manchester's mill district, proud of her invisibility and convinced history happens elsewhere. A chance remark from a printer suggests the war is closer than she thinks. Emotional beat: comfortable complacency beginning to crack.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Familiar Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A gaunt stranger named Callum arrives at the workshop carrying a letter in her dead brother Edmund's handwriting, asking about 'the compass.' She denies everything, but the letter's cipher matches work only Edmund knew. Emotional beat: grief reopened; disbelief warring with hope.

chapters.title: What the Workshop Hides
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with an interlude from Callum's journal. She searches the workshop her brother helped build and finds the first layer of the hidden treaty beneath the floorboards. Callum reveals he was Edmund's fellow courier—and that Edmund may be alive. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering her ordinary life was always part of something larger.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Her Loyalty
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her mentor Aldous Vane, head of the courier network, warns her to burn what she found and sail on the morning tide like everyone else. His fear seems like wisdom until she notices he has already sent word to someone. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against dawning suspicion.

chapters.title: Mill Smoke and Watchers
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Hunted through the mill district by regime agents, Callum evades capture using routes Edmund once mapped, realizing too late that his own arrival was tracked. He chooses to lead the watchers away from Mirabel. Emotional beat: guilt transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Cipher
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Working alone through the night, she cracks the second layer and learns the treaty trades the republic's treasury for sanctuary—a betrayal dressed as rescue. Edmund's handwriting appears again, warning her not to trust the messenger. Emotional beat: the sickening collision of loyalty and truth.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Confronted, Vane admits he sold the route to save his daughter held abroad, and begs Mirabel to let the ship sail without the treaty. Agents close on the workshop. Emotional beat: pity and fury entangled; no clean villains, only impossible choices.

chapters.title: The Night the Looms Stopped
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The mill workers, whom she has passed for years without seeing, shelter her and finish the decoding together—the final key lives in the collective memory of the district itself. The workshop burns as they escape. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not assumed; the climax of shared purpose.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. At the docks, agents intercept them; Vane redeems himself by dying to buy passage, and Callum boards with the treaty as the ship slips out on the tide. Through the crowd, Mirabel glimpses a figure with Edmund's walk who does not turn around. Emotional beat: sacrifice, release, and a deliberately unanswered question.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Home
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, one year later. The refugees are settled; the republic is gone but its people endure, and Mirabel runs the workshop as a school for the district's children. She keeps Edmund's unfinished letter, choosing the living over the ghost. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—history happened to her, and she answered it.
